title: Contar una historia
goal: Tell a short story, choosing between the preterite and the imperfect.

lessons.title: The scene and the event
lessons.notes:
A story needs both past tenses, and each has a job:
**Imperfect** = the **scene**: what was going on, what things were like, the background. It's the film set.
**Preterite** = the **events**: what happened next, one step at a time. It's the action.
**Estaba en casa cuando sonó el teléfono.** = I was at home when the phone rang.
"Was at home" is the scene (imperfect); "rang" interrupts it (preterite).
Rules of thumb:
- Could you say "was ...-ing" or "used to"? -> **imperfect**
- Is it a single completed thing, with a start or end you can point to? -> **preterite**
- **de repente** (suddenly) is almost always followed by the preterite.
**Hacía sol cuando salimos.** = It was sunny when we went out.

sentences.es: Estaba en casa cuando sonó el teléfono.
sentences.en: I was at home when the phone rang.

sentences.es: Llovía cuando salí del trabajo.
sentences.en: It was raining when I left work.
accept_en: It was raining when I left the office.

sentences.es: Hacía sol y fuimos a la playa.
sentences.en: It was sunny and we went to the beach.

sentences.es: De repente, un perro entró en la cocina.
sentences.en: Suddenly a dog came into the kitchen.
accept_en: Suddenly, a dog came into the kitchen.
All of a sudden a dog came into the kitchen.
Suddenly a dog went into the kitchen.

sentences.es: Mi hermana estaba triste cuando llegué.
sentences.en: My sister was sad when I arrived.
accept_en: My sister was sad when I got there.
My sister was sad when I got home.

sentences.es: Cuando entré, todos estaban en la sala.
sentences.en: When I came in, everyone was in the living room.
accept_en: When I went in, everyone was in the living room.
When I came in, they were all in the lounge room.

sentences.es: El teléfono sonó a las tres de la mañana.
sentences.en: The phone rang at three in the morning.

sentences.es: Alguien abrió la puerta de repente.
sentences.en: Someone suddenly opened the door.
accept_en: Somebody opened the door all of a sudden.

lessons.title: Setting the scene
lessons.notes:
Descriptions in the past - time, weather, place, people, feelings, age - go in the **imperfect**:
**Era de noche.** (It was night.) · **Eran las once.** · **Había mucha gente.** (There were a lot of people.) · **Estaba nervioso.** · **Tenía veinte años.**
**la gente** (people) is **singular** in Spanish: **la gente es simpática**.
**parecer** = to seem / look: **parecía cansado** (he looked tired).
**llevar** in the imperfect describes what someone was wearing: **Llevaba un abrigo negro.**
Put a few of these together and you've painted the picture before anything happens.

items.en: there were a lot of people

sentences.es: Era de noche y hacía mucho frío.
sentences.en: It was night and it was very cold.
accept_en: It was dark and very cold.
It was night-time and it was really cold.

sentences.es: En la plaza había mucha gente.
sentences.en: There were a lot of people in the square.
accept_en: In the square there were lots of people.
There were many people in the square.

sentences.es: El hombre parecía muy nervioso.
sentences.en: The man seemed very nervous.

sentences.es: La mujer llevaba un vestido negro.
sentences.en: The woman was wearing a black dress.
accept_en: The woman wore a black dress.

sentences.es: El pueblo era pequeño y tranquilo.
sentences.en: The town was small and quiet.
accept_en: The village was small and quiet.
The town was small and peaceful.

sentences.es: Tenía veinte años y vivía en Lima.
sentences.en: I was twenty and I lived in Lima.
accept_en: I was twenty years old and lived in Lima.
I was twenty and was living in Lima.

sentences.es: Eran las once y todos estaban cansados.
sentences.en: It was eleven and everyone was tired.
accept_en: It was eleven o'clock and everyone was tired.
It was eleven and they were all tired.

sentences.es: La gente parece muy simpática aquí.
sentences.en: The people seem very nice here.

lessons.title: I was doing it when...
lessons.notes:
To stress that something was **in progress**, use **estar** in the imperfect + the **-ing form** (the gerund):
-ar -> **-ando**: hablando, cocinando
-er / -ir -> **-iendo**: comiendo, saliendo
A few change: **leyendo** (reading), **durmiendo** (sleeping, o -> u), **diciendo** (saying).
**Estaba leyendo cuando llegaste.** = I was reading when you arrived.
This is the classic interruption: the long action in **estaba + -ando / -iendo**, the short one in the preterite.
The same form works in the present: **Estoy cocinando.** = I'm cooking (right now).

sentences.es: Estaba leyendo cuando llegaste.
sentences.en: I was reading when you arrived.
accept_en: I was reading when you got here.
I was reading when you got home.

sentences.es: Estaba durmiendo cuando sonó el despertador.
sentences.en: I was sleeping when the alarm went off.
accept_en: I was asleep when the alarm clock rang.
I was sleeping when the alarm clock went off.

sentences.es: Estábamos comiendo cuando oímos un ruido.
sentences.en: We were eating when we heard a noise.
accept_en: We were having lunch when we heard a noise.
We were eating when we heard a sound.

sentences.es: Los niños estaban jugando en el jardín.
sentences.en: The children were playing in the garden.
accept_en: The kids were playing in the garden.
The children were playing in the yard.

sentences.es: Ahora no puedo, estoy cocinando.
sentences.en: I can't right now, I'm cooking.

sentences.es: ¿Qué estabas haciendo a las diez?
sentences.en: What were you doing at ten?
accept_en: What were you doing at ten o'clock?

sentences.es: Mi papá estaba trabajando cuando tuve la llamada.
sentences.en: My dad was working when I got the call.
accept_en: My dad was working when I had the call.
My father was working when I got the phone call.

sentences.es: ¿Oíste ese ruido?
sentences.en: Did you hear that noise?

sentences.es: El bebé duerme muy bien.
sentences.en: The baby sleeps very well.

lessons.title: Once upon a time
lessons.notes:
Linking words carry a story along:
**un día** (one day) · **al principio** (at first) · **entonces** (then, so) · **luego / después** · **por eso** (that's why) · **al final** (in the end)
**contar** (o -> ue) = to tell (a story) and also to count: **Te cuento una historia.**
A tiny story, with the tenses marked:
**Un día estaba** (imp.) **en el parque. Hacía** (imp.) **calor. De repente vi** (pret.) **a un amigo. Al final comimos** (pret.) **juntos.**
Notice the shape: background first in the imperfect, then the chain of events in the preterite.

items.note: e -> ie: pierdo. Also to miss a bus or plane.

sentences.es: Te cuento una historia.
sentences.en: I'll tell you a story.
accept_en: Let me tell you a story.

sentences.es: Un día estaba en el parque con mi perro.
sentences.en: One day I was in the park with my dog.
accept_en: One day I was at the park with my dog.

sentences.es: Al principio no entendía nada.
sentences.en: At first I didn't understand anything.
accept_en: In the beginning I didn't understand anything.

sentences.es: Perdí las llaves y por eso llegué tarde.
sentences.en: I lost the keys and that's why I arrived late.
accept_en: I lost my keys, so I was late.
I lost the keys and that's why I was late.
I lost my keys and that's why I got there late.

sentences.es: Estaba cansado, entonces me acosté.
sentences.en: I was tired, so I went to bed.
accept_en: I was tired, so then I went to bed.

sentences.es: Al final comimos juntos en un restaurante.
sentences.en: In the end we ate together at a restaurant.
accept_en: In the end we ate together in a restaurant.
Finally we had a meal together at a restaurant.

sentences.es: Mi abuelo contaba historias muy divertidas.
sentences.en: My grandfather used to tell very funny stories.
accept_en: My grandad told really funny stories.
My grandfather used to tell very fun stories.

sentences.es: ¿Qué pasó al final?
sentences.en: What happened in the end?

sentences.es: Fuimos juntos al concierto.
sentences.en: We went to the concert together.

lessons.title: Knew or found out?
lessons.notes:
A few verbs change meaning between the two tenses, because the preterite marks the **moment it started**:
**conocía** = I knew (someone, a place) · **conocí** = I **met** (for the first time)
**sabía** = I knew (a fact) · **supe** = I **found out**
**quería** = I wanted · **no quise / no quiso** = I / he **refused**
**podía** = I could (in general) · **pude** = I **managed to**
**Conocí a mi esposa en 2015.** = I met my wife in 2015.
**Sabía la verdad.** = I knew the truth.
Remember the little **a** before people: **conocí a Luis**.

items.note: conozco, conoces... Preterite: conocí = I met.
One piece of news; las noticias = the news (on TV).

sentences.es: Conocí a mi esposa en una fiesta.
sentences.en: I met my wife at a party.

sentences.es: No conocía a nadie en la ciudad.
sentences.en: I didn't know anyone in the city.
accept_en: I knew nobody in the city.
I didn't know anybody in the city.

sentences.es: Ayer supe la noticia.
sentences.en: I found out the news yesterday.
accept_en: Yesterday I found out the news.

sentences.es: Sabía la verdad, pero no dije nada.
sentences.en: I knew the truth, but I didn't say anything.
accept_en: I knew the truth but said nothing.
I knew the truth, but I said nothing.

sentences.es: Mi hijo no quiso comer.
sentences.en: My son refused to eat.
accept_en: My son didn't want to eat.

sentences.es: ¿Dónde conociste a tu novio?
sentences.en: Where did you meet your boyfriend?

sentences.es: ¿Sabes la verdad?
sentences.en: Do you know the truth?

sentences.es: No quise ir, pero al final fui.
sentences.en: I refused to go, but in the end I went.
accept_en: I didn't want to go, but in the end I went.

sentences.es: ¿Conoces Buenos Aires?
sentences.en: Have you been to Buenos Aires?
